tasks.short: Write and send letters about collective agreements, disputes, conciliation and contract interpretation.

steps.what: Register the correspondence request and link it to the case.
Retrieve the current agreement, relevant clauses and previous correspondence.
Agree the intended position, concessions and tone with the responsible manager.
Draft the letter using the agreed position and relevant clauses.

loop.input: Approved correspondence brief, letter template and permission-filtered source bundle.
loop.output: Draft letter with clause references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate names, dates and quoted clauses against sources; the specialist checks meaning and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting sources return the work to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover routine wording, but disputed interpretations and negotiating intent require case-specific prose.

steps.what: Review legal meaning and commitments, then approve the final letter.
Send the approved letter to the agreed recipients.
Save the sent letter and update the correspondence history.

tasks.design: A case record in {WORKFLOW} links requests from {EMAIL} to approved agreement versions in {DOCS} or {CLM}. Templates handle standard letters; a bounded drafting loop handles case-specific wording with source references. The responsible manager approves the exact text and recipients before {EMAIL} sends it and updates the case history.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement versions and correspondence were scattered. Templates could not express disputed interpretations or negotiating intent.
tasks.enabler_now: Source retrieval, document assembly and approval routing are established techniques. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, while bounded drafting handles variable prose.
tasks.still_hard: A letter can concede rights or change a negotiating position. National rules, agreement validity, confidentiality and GDPR requirements still need careful interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what a sentence commits the employer to and how the other party will receive it.

ambition.what: Pre-negotiation clause clarification clinic for line managers

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting files and formatting letters, leaving time for clause clarification before disputes escalate. Authority to make commitments stays with the existing signatory.

reach.task: Prepare employee notices affected by collective agreement changes.
reach.learn: Translate approved clauses into notices without adding commitments; learn version control and confidentiality.

evidence.claim: Templates, source retrieval and approval routing can reduce correspondence preparation; no direct labor-relations implementation is documented in the digest.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent sources and a partial refund, supporting explicit source verification.

assumptions: Steps and time shares are planning estimates for a mid-size European employer, not measured results.
The representative path concerns agreement clarification or amendment; dispute letters follow the same pattern in complaint-to-resolution.
The document-heavy prior fits preparation, but its high automation probability overstates delegation of position-setting and approval.
Routine letters use templates without a model; the loop applies only to variable prose.
Build ranges cover one language and jurisdiction, including access and applicable national employee consultation.
Approval binds the letter version and recipient list; changing either requires renewed approval.
unknowns: Which role can approve letters and legally bind the employer?
Are authoritative agreements versioned and searchable in {DOCS} or {CLM}?
What correspondence volume, languages and amendment types occur?
What access, retention and employee consultation arrangements already exist?
research_questions: Which letter types can use fixed templates without interpretive drafting?
Which national rules govern agreement amendments, service and representative consultation?
Can source references reliably distinguish current clauses from superseded ones?
new_work: Review variable drafts and resolve missing or conflicting sources.
Maintain templates, agreement versions and approval delegations.
Check failed delivery and incorrect recipient mappings.
Maintain access controls, retention settings and connector permissions.

tasks.short: Arrange grievance hearings and related meetings, including participants, timing, notices and papers.

steps.what: Check participants, deadlines and access needs against the grievance procedure.
Ask participants for availability and practical requirements.
Compare availability, rooms and procedural deadlines to find suitable slots.
Resolve clashes, accommodation requests and disputed timing with participants.
Book the hearing and issue the formal notice.
Assemble the agenda and authorized hearing papers.
Share authorized papers and send hearing reminders.

tasks.design: Configure availability requests and notices in {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}, using neutral calendar titles and structured hearing requirements. A deterministic check finds slots within approved deadlines, while {DOCS} assembles papers from an authorized document list. The specialist resolves contested timing and approves formal notices and paper distribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Calendar availability did not capture representation rights, procedural deadlines or confidential document access. Coordination depended on repeated mailbox exchanges.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling, forms and approval features handle most of the work. Small deterministic checks can add procedural constraints without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Availability does not establish fair notice or reasonable accommodation. National rules and agreement procedures can make apparently convenient dates unacceptable.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a timing objection reflects a real participation barrier and negotiate a fair arrangement.

ambition.what: Participant hearing-readiness check before formal notice

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time chasing dates and more time resolving participation barriers before hearings. Routine slot selection can move to the assistant under existing delegation; contested timing remains with the specialist.

reach.learn: Apply notice periods, representation requirements, accessibility arrangements and document permissions.

evidence.claim: Availability collection, calendar booking, template notices and reminders are established configurable capabilities.
Constraint checks can automate slot comparison while leaving contested timing and participation rights to people.

assumptions: Steps and time shares are estimates, not measured results.
Mailbox coordination is substantial here; the prior's large meeting share is reduced because conducting the hearing is a separate task.
Participant lists and deadlines are confirmed before automated availability requests.
Routine availability requests contain neutral wording and disclose no grievance details.
Participants can use a scheduling form or provide availability through the assistant.
Build ranges include access and applicable national employee consultation; external waiting time can extend rollout.
unknowns: Who schedules hearings today, and who may confirm dates?
Which notice periods and representation requirements apply?
Can external representatives use availability forms?
Are suitable rooms, interpreters and accessibility services bookable through {CALENDAR}?
Which papers may each participant receive?
research_questions: Can existing {CALENDAR} configuration satisfy the constraints before custom code is added?
Which deadline calculations require human interpretation rather than a fixed rule?
How should postponements invalidate notices, reminders and previously shared papers?
new_work: Handle nonresponses, disputed dates and accommodation requests.
Maintain procedural calendars, templates and participant permissions.
Review notices and paper distribution before release.
Resolve failed invitations and changes after confirmation.

tasks.short: Review proposed disciplinary actions for evidence, fair procedure and proportionality, then approve or reject them.

steps.what: Gather the proposed action, employment records and supporting evidence.
Read the evidence and reconstruct events, disputed facts and missing information.

loop.output: Source-linked chronology, attributed allegations, contradictions and missing facts.
loop.check: Validate dates and source links; the specialist checks material events, omissions and attribution.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; unreadable or conflicting evidence goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence arrives as free-text accounts and letters; fixed fields cannot reconstruct their chronology.

steps.what: Check procedural requirements and flag gaps before substantive review.
Hear the employee and manager, clarify contested facts and consider mitigating circumstances.
Assess proportionality and approve, revise or reject the proposed action.
Write the decision record and implementation instructions.
Confirm the record, enter the approved decision and route implementation instructions.

tasks.design: A restricted case workspace links evidence from {HCM} and {DOCS}; a bounded extraction loop drafts a source-linked chronology without recommending sanctions. Deterministic checks flag missing procedural steps, and templates assemble the person's decision reasons. The authorized manager makes the substantive decision and approves the exact record before {WORKFLOW} updates {HCM} and routes implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered and procedural checks were manual. Sanction decisions depend on disputed facts, context and fair treatment that fixed rules cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Permissioned retrieval and structured extraction can reduce preparation work. Ordinary rule checks and document assembly handle the surrounding paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, proportionality and discrimination concerns remain human judgements. GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated significant decisions [S20]; assess the EU AI Act's employment provisions against intended use [S17] and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh contested accounts, hear mitigating circumstances and take responsibility for a decision affecting someone's livelihood.

ambition.what: Early procedural repair consultation for line managers

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconstructing files and can help managers correct procedural defects before a decision meeting. Final disciplinary authority stays with the authorized manager; any power to pause incomplete cases requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Review potential unequal treatment in disciplinary procedures.
reach.learn: Recognize discrimination indicators and apply lawful, confidential comparison methods.

evidence.claim: Source-linked extraction can assist chronology preparation, but its completeness requires human review.
Deterministic procedural checks and template records can support disciplinary review without deciding culpability or sanctions.
The digest provides no documented disciplinary-review automation case; savings and decision quality remain unvalidated.

assumptions: Steps and time shares are planning estimates, not measured results.
The human classification is retained for substantive review; preparation and recording can still change.
The authorized decision-maker is represented by the human resources manager; local delegation may differ.
The extraction loop attributes allegations and does not infer guilt, rank employees or recommend sanctions.
Procedural rules have approved versions; ambiguous checks remain with the specialist.
Decision reasons are entered by the person in structured fields before deterministic document assembly.
Build ranges include access, GDPR assessment and applicable national employee consultation; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve reprimands, suspensions and terminations?
Which national rules and collective agreements govern each employee group?
Where are evidence, employee responses and prior decisions held?
What sensitive data, retention periods and access restrictions apply?
What employee consultation and data protection assessments already cover the proposed use?
research_questions: Does the intended use fall within EU AI Act employment high-risk provisions?
What GDPR assessment is required for this processing and its sensitive data?
Can extraction preserve material contradictions and distinguish allegations from established facts?
Which procedural checks can be encoded without implying that a sanction is justified?
new_work: Check chronology omissions, attribution errors and unsupported statements.
Resolve procedural exceptions and incomplete evidence.
Maintain approved procedure versions and access controls.
Validate implementation routing against the approved decision.
Monitor extraction errors and reassess the system when its intended use changes.

tasks.short: Select and appoint a mediator or arbitrator acceptable to the parties in a labor dispute.

steps.what: Interpret appointment clauses and define the dispute's selection requirements.
Compile candidates from approved rosters and previous appointment records.
Request availability, fees and conflict disclosures from potential appointees.
Discuss neutrality, experience and suitability with employee representatives.
Agree the nominee and appointment terms with the dispute parties.
Prepare the appointment document from agreed terms.
Review and sign the appointment document.
File the signed appointment and update the case record.

tasks.design: A small roster in {WORKFLOW} links approved profiles and appointment history in {DOCS}; deterministic filters apply the specialist's stated requirements. Approved inquiries go through {EMAIL}, and templates produce the appointment document for human agreement and signing in {ESIGN}. Selection remains a discussion between the parties, with no automated suitability score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selection was infrequent and depended on trust, local appointment rules and personal knowledge. Roster information and prior terms were difficult to reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable records app, structured inquiry form and document template can handle administration cheaply. This path needs no model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Formal qualifications and a conflict disclosure do not establish perceived neutrality. National rules, contractual appointment mechanisms and the parties' willingness to accept a nominee remain decisive.
tasks.human_edge: Find someone both parties will trust to conduct a fair process, including when their preferences conflict.

ambition.what: Early mediation appointment option for emerging disputes

tasks.altitude: The specialist can spend less time rebuilding rosters and appointment paperwork and more time exploring mediation before positions harden. Authority to appoint or bind the parties does not change.

reach.task: Choose the escalation route for an unresolved employee dispute.
reach.learn: Distinguish mediation from arbitration and understand appointment authority, fees and confidentiality.

evidence.claim: Structured rosters, fixed filters, inquiry templates and document assembly can reduce appointment administration.
Trust and joint acceptability require human discussion; the digest provides no direct mediator-selection automation case.

assumptions: Steps and time shares are planning estimates, not measured results.
The representative path uses joint appointment; some national or contractual mechanisms designate an appointing body instead.
The prior correctly identifies a human selection task; its model-needed probability is rejected for structured administration.
Roster filters use explicit requirements, never inferred reputation or employee-related predictions.
Candidates confirm current availability and conflicts; historical records are not treated as clearance.
Nonstandard appointment clauses go to manual drafting.
Build ranges assume reuse of existing case tooling and include access and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Is there an approved roster or prescribed appointing body?
Who must consent to the nominee and sign the appointment?
Which qualifications, languages and jurisdictions are required?
How often are appointments made, and would shared tooling justify the build?
Which profile and conflict information may lawfully be retained?
research_questions: Which appointment mechanisms apply under national rules and collective agreements?
Can fixed filters capture requirements without ranking perceived neutrality?
What information may be disclosed before a candidate completes conflict checks?
new_work: Refresh roster details and record candidate-confirmed availability.
Review conflict disclosures and disputed suitability.
Maintain appointment templates and signing delegations.
Handle appointments that require an external appointing body.
Remove stale or excessive personal information from the roster.

role.altitude: The specialist spends less of the week assembling files, chasing dates and reproducing documents. More time goes to early dispute prevention, fair participation and substantive judgement; bargaining, disciplinary decisions and appointment authority remain with authorized people.
reach: Help human resources specialists translate agreement changes into accurate employee notices.
Help human resources assistants coordinate confidential meetings with procedural safeguards.
Work with equal opportunity officers on fair disciplinary procedures.
Help human resources managers consider mediation earlier in unresolved disputes.
skills_to_grow: Translate procedures into explicit checks without turning judgement into a score.
Verify source-linked summaries and distinguish allegations from established facts.
Design confidential case access, retention and approval controls.
Understand GDPR, relevant EU AI Act provisions and applicable national consultation rules.
Facilitate difficult conversations and explain the consequences of proposed commitments.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an early dispute-prevention service combining clause clarification, hearing-readiness checks, procedural repair and mediation options. Use shared case tooling to prepare those interventions while people retain decisions affecting rights, employment and negotiated commitments.
